cards.title: NCLEX Success for Internationally Qualified Nurses
cards.body: Your comprehensive guide to upskilling, exam preparation, and launching a rewarding nursing career in the United States.

cards.title: What Is the NCLEX?
cards.body: The National Council Licensure Examination

bullets.label: The NCLEX is the standardised licensing exam
bullets.text: The NCLEX is the standardised licensing exam required for all nurses wishing to practise in the USA and Canada. For internationally qualified nurses (IQNs), passing the NCLEX is the critical gateway to professional recognition abroad.

bullets.label: Administered by the National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
Tests clinical judgement, not just memorisation

cards.title: Who Is This Programme For?
cards.body: 🌍 Internationally Trained Nurses

bullets.label: Qualified nurses from outside the US seeking licensure and career advancement.
Nurses wanting to refresh clinical knowledge and align with US standards of practice.
Those preparing to sit the NCLEX-RN or NCLEX-PN for the very first time.
Adaptive format adjusts to your ability level
Covering all core areas of nursing practice
Understanding the exam's structure helps you
bullets.text: Understanding the exam's structure helps you study smarter, not just harder. The CAT format means every question matters equally.

cards.title: NCLEX-RN: The 8 Client Needs Categories
cards.body: Where to Focus Your Revision

bullets.label: The NCLEX tests nursing knowledge across a
bullets.text: The NCLEX tests nursing knowledge across a broad spectrum. The largest weighted categories are Management of Care and Pharmacological Therapies — allocate the most study time here.

bullets.label: Physiological Integrity accounts for nearly 50% of all questions combined.

cards.title: Understanding the Next Generation NCLEX (NGN)
cards.body: Since April 2023, the NCLEX has moved to the Next Generation NCLEX (NGN) format, emphasising clinical judgement over rote recall.

cards.title: ELIGIBILITY
cards.body: Steps to NCLEX Eligibility for IQNs

bullets.label: The pathway varies slightly by US state.
bullets.text: The pathway varies slightly by US state. Research your target state's Board of Nursing requirements early — some states have additional documentation steps for IQNs.

cards.title: Credential Evaluation: What You Need
cards.body: Recognised Credential Bodies

bullets.label: Most state boards require evaluation by an approved agency before granting eligibility.
Gather original transcripts, nursing licence, and programme details. Processing can take 3–6 months — start early.
Take a diagnostic practice test to identify weak areas across the 8 content categories.
Most IQNs benefit from 8–12 weeks of structured preparation. Create a weekly study schedule.
Practise NGN-style case studies, not just multiple-choice questions. Think through the NCSBN model.
Do at least 75–100 practice questions daily and review every incorrect answer in detail.

cards.title: Top Revision Resources
cards.body: Saunders Comprehensive Review

bullets.label: The gold-standard textbook for NCLEX prep. Covers all content areas with rationale-based Q&A.
High-quality online question banks with detailed explanations and performance analytics.
Official NCSBN prep course including NGN-style items and clinical judgement case studies.
Joining an IQN study community reduces isolation and boosts accountability and knowledge sharing.

cards.title: CORE CLINICAL KNOWLEDGE
cards.body: High-Yield Clinical Topics to Master

bullets.label: Drug classes, side effects, priority interventions — especially cardiac, psychiatric, and pain meds.
IV therapy, imbalances (hypokalaemia, hypernatraemia), and nursing responses.
Labour stages, foetal monitoring, postpartum complications, and newborn assessment.
Therapeutic communication, psychiatric disorders, medication management, and crisis intervention.
ABC framework, Maslow's hierarchy, and safe scope of practice for UAPs and LPNs.
Standard and transmission-based precautions, PPE selection, and surgical asepsis.

cards.title: Mastering Clinical Judgement Questions
cards.body: NGN questions are scenario-based and require you to think like an experienced nurse, not just recall facts. Common new item types include:

bullets.label: Select all correct answers — partial credit scoring applies.
Rank interventions or match conditions to findings.
Evaluate multiple options across multiple conditions simultaneously.
Link patient conditions, actions, and outcomes in a structured format.

cards.title: EXAM DAY
cards.body: On Exam Day: What to Expect

bullets.label: Bring valid government-issued photo ID — name must match ATT exactly
Arrive at least 30 minutes early for check-in and biometrics
No personal belongings, phones, or notes permitted in the testing room
The exam stops when the algorithm is confident in your pass/fail status
Results typically available within 48 hours via Quick Results
Trust your preparation. If you reach 145
bullets.text: Trust your preparation. If you reach 145 questions, that is not a bad sign — stay focused on each question independently.

cards.title: Life After NCLEX: Your Career Path in the US
cards.body: Obtain State Nursing Licence

bullets.label: Receive your RN or PN licence from the state board upon passing.
Target hospitals, clinics, or community health settings aligned with your speciality and experience.
Consider certifications in ICU, paediatrics, oncology, or mental health to advance your career.
Many US employers support RNs pursuing a BSN or MSN for leadership and advanced practice roles.

cards.title: Your Journey Starts Now
cards.body: You have the knowledge. Now earn the licence.

bullets.label: Thousands of internationally qualified nurses
bullets.text: Thousands of internationally qualified nurses have successfully passed the NCLEX and built extraordinary careers in the United States. With the right preparation, resources, and mindset — you are next.

bullets.label: Enrol in a structured NCLEX prep programme
Sit your exam with confidence and clarity

decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 6 - Level 1 - Section 1 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS)
cards.body: Programme 6 · Level 1 – Qualified Nurse

cards.title: Section 1: Understanding Pregnancy & Antenatal Care
cards.body: Why Antenatal Nursing Matters

bullets.label: Pregnancy brings major physiological and emotional changes. Most are normal adaptations — but some findings signal risk.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you should be able to:

bullets.label: Describe common adaptations of pregnancy across body systems
Complete a structured basic antenatal assessment
Distinguish normal discomforts from warning signs requiring action
Provide evidence-based guidance for a healthy pregnancy

cards.title: Physiological Adaptations in Pregnancy
cards.body: Pregnancy affects multiple organ systems simultaneously. Understanding expected changes helps nurses distinguish normal findings from those requiring escalation.

bullets.label: Increased blood volume; mild anaemia; heart rate rises
Mild breathlessness; diaphragm elevation; increased oxygen demand
Urinary frequency; increased GFR; glycosuria possible
Nausea, heartburn; insulin resistance; elevated thyroid activity

cards.title: Antenatal Assessment
cards.body: Physical

bullets.label: A structured assessment at every visit enables
bullets.text: A structured assessment at every visit enables early identification of anaemia, diabetes, infection, hypertension, and fetal growth concerns.

cards.title: Nutrition & Health Promotion
cards.body: Key Health Education Topics

bullets.label: Adequate folate and iron supplementation as recommended
Moderate physical activity; adequate rest and sleep
Flu and whooping cough vaccines as per schedule
No smoking, alcohol, or harmful substances

cards.title: ⚠️ Pregnancy Danger Signs
cards.body: The following symptoms require prompt evaluation — never dismiss them as routine pregnancy discomforts.

bullets.label: May indicate hypertensive disorders; act urgently
Rapid oedema of face, hands or feet
Could signal placental abruption or preterm labour
Risk of infection; reduced fetal movement also requires urgent review

cards.title: Clinical Example: Mrs Rao at 32 Weeks
cards.body: Presentation

bullets.label: Mrs Rao presents at 32 weeks reporting a severe headache, blurred vision, and swelling of her hands.
Hypertension is a key indicator of pre-eclampsia
Monitor fetal heart rate and movement
Do NOT dismiss symptoms as normal discomforts

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Know the Difference

bullets.label: Distinguish expected physiological changes from danger signs requiring escalation
Antenatal care addresses both maternal and fetal wellbeing at every visit
Encourage early booking and consistent attendance at scheduled antenatal visits
Severe headache, bleeding, or reduced fetal movement — act without delay

cards.title: GNPS Programme 6 — Section 1 Complete
cards.body: "Healthy beginnings start with skilled, compassionate, and vigilant nursing care."

bullets.label: Proceed to Section 2: Labour, Birth, and Intrapartum Care
Review danger signs, assessment parameters, and priority nursing actions
How would you apply these skills in your clinical setting?

decks.title: Nursing Care During Labour and Birth
decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 6 - Level 1 - Section 2 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Nursing Care During Labour and Birth
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS) · Program 6 · Level 1 · Section 2

cards.title: Introduction
cards.body: Labour is a dynamic, evolving process that demands continuous, holistic assessment throughout. The nurse monitors the woman's physical and emotional state, fetal wellbeing, contraction patterns, pain levels, and labour progress at every stage.

bullets.label: Escalating promptly when labour deviates from expected patterns

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Describe the stages and key features of labour from onset to recovery.
Assess maternal and fetal wellbeing accurately throughout labour.
Provide supportive interventions and appropriate pain-relief options.
Recognise findings that require immediate escalation and intervention.

cards.title: The Four Stages of Labour
cards.body: Nursing priorities shift significantly as labour advances through each stage. Understanding the hallmarks of each stage enables timely, appropriate care.

bullets.label: Cervical dilation from 0–10 cm; includes latent and active phases
Full dilation to birth of the baby; pushing and descent
Delivery of the placenta and membranes following birth
Immediate postpartum recovery; monitoring for haemorrhage and stability

cards.title: The Five Ps of Labour
cards.body: Labour progress is shaped by five interrelated factors. A thorough assessment considers all five together:

bullets.label: Passenger: Fetal position, lie, presentation, and size
Passageway: Pelvic shape, dimensions, and soft tissue
Powers: Contraction frequency, duration, and intensity
Position: Maternal posture and mobility during labour
Psyche: Emotional readiness, anxiety, and coping ability
All five Ps interact — a difficulty in one can affect the others and alter the course of labour.

cards.title: Fetal & Contraction Monitoring
cards.body: What to Monitor

bullets.label: Baseline rate, variability, accelerations, and decelerations
Frequency, duration, strength, and resting tone between contractions
BP, pulse, temperature, urinalysis, and pain score
Cervical dilation, effacement, fetal descent, and station
Frequency of assessment is guided by the
bullets.text: Frequency of assessment is guided by the woman's risk level and local policy. Abnormal patterns always require prompt, decisive action.

cards.title: Comfort & Support Measures
cards.body: Effective comfort care integrates both non-pharmacological and pharmacological approaches, always guided by the woman's informed choices and preferences.

bullets.label: Encourage frequent position changes and upright postures to aid fetal descent and reduce pain.
Guided breathing and relaxation techniques reduce anxiety and improve pain tolerance.
Back massage, warm compresses, and water therapy provide significant physical comfort.
Entonox, opioids, epidural anaesthesia — offered clearly with balanced information.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Recognising an Abnormal FHR Pattern
cards.body: Scenario: During active labour, late decelerations of the fetal heart rate are noted repeatedly following contractions on the CTG monitor.

bullets.label: Late decelerations are never observed passively
bullets.text: Late decelerations are never observed passively — they signal potential uteroplacental insufficiency and require immediate action.

bullets.label: Reposition the woman — left lateral or hands-and-knees
Stop oxytocin infusion immediately per local policy
Increase frequency of maternal and fetal observations
Call for urgent medical review without delay
Prepare for further intervention — theatre readiness if required

cards.title: NCLEX-Style Practice Questions
cards.body: Test your understanding of labour and birth nursing care with these scenario-based questions.

bullets.label: A nurse notes late decelerations on the CTG.
bullets.text: A nurse notes late decelerations on the CTG. What is the priority intervention? (A) Increase IV fluids (B) Reposition the woman (C) Administer oxygen mask (D) Call the doctor first)

bullets.label: Which of the Five Ps refers to the strength and frequency of uterine contractions during labour?
During the fourth stage of labour, what is the nurse's primary focus of assessment?
Answers: Q1 – B (repositioning is the immediate
bullets.text: Answers: Q1 – B (repositioning is the immediate priority); Q2 – Powers; Q3 – Haemorrhage, vital sign stability, and uterine tone.

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Carry these principles into every labour and birth encounter:

bullets.label: Always evaluate the mother and fetus as a unit — never in isolation.
Promote movement, comfort, and the woman's right to informed decision-making.
Know the features of abnormal FHR patterns and act — do not wait and watch.
When labour progress or fetal wellbeing is concerning, escalate without hesitation.
Section 2 complete. Proceed to Section 3: Postpartum Care and Complications.

decks.title: Postnatal Recovery and Maternal Wellbeing
decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 6 - Level 1 - Section 3 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Postnatal Recovery and Maternal Wellbeing
cards.body: GNPS PROGRAMME 6 · SECTION 3

bullets.label: Global Nursing Professional Series · Level 1 – Qualified Nurse

cards.title: What You Will Learn
cards.body: By the end of Section 3, you will be able to confidently support mothers through postnatal recovery.

bullets.label: Perform a structured postnatal maternal assessment from head to toe.
Identify haemorrhage, infection, thromboembolism and mental-health concerns early.
Promote breastfeeding, maternal comfort and effective latch technique.
Promote emotional wellbeing and prepare families for a confident transition home.

cards.title: Postnatal Maternal Assessment
cards.body: A systematic head-to-toe approach ensures no concern is missed during the critical postnatal period.

bullets.label: Temperature, pulse, blood pressure and respiratory rate at regular intervals.
Check uterine tone, position and descent. Assess lochia colour, volume and odour.
Inspect for redness, oedema, bruising, discharge or wound breakdown.
Encourage voiding, monitor output and assess early mobilisation for thrombosis prevention.

cards.title: Postpartum Haemorrhage (PPH)
cards.body: PRIORITY: EMERGENCY RESPONSE

bullets.label: PPH is one of the leading causes of maternal mortality worldwide. Early recognition is critical.
Treat heavy postpartum bleeding as an emergency. Do not delay escalation.

cards.title: PPH: Nursing Response
cards.body: Act swiftly and systematically. Every minute matters when haemorrhage is suspected.

bullets.label: Remain with the woman throughout. Document all
bullets.text: Remain with the woman throughout. Document all findings, interventions and timings accurately, and reassess continuously until the situation is stabilised.

cards.title: Infection & Thromboembolism
cards.body: Postnatal infection and thromboembolism can develop rapidly. Vigilant monitoring and prompt escalation are essential.

bullets.label: Low oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry
Any of these signs require urgent clinical review. Do not wait to see if symptoms resolve.

cards.title: Emotional Adaptation & Mental Wellbeing
cards.body: The postnatal period brings profound emotional change. Nurses play a key role in distinguishing normal adjustment from clinical concern.

bullets.label: Mild emotional lability ("baby blues") in the first few days — typically self-resolving.
Persistent low mood, severe anxiety or inability to cope beyond two weeks — requires timely referral.
Thoughts of harm to self or baby — a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate escalation.

cards.title: Supporting Breastfeeding & Maternal Comfort
cards.body: Early, consistent nursing support significantly improves breastfeeding outcomes and maternal confidence.

bullets.label: Assist mother to achieve a deep latch and comfortable feeding position to prevent nipple trauma.
Encourage feeding on demand — typically 8–12 times per 24 hours in the newborn period.
Assess for engorgement, blocked ducts or mastitis and provide evidence-based guidance promptly.
Ensure adequate analgesia for perineal or caesarean wound pain to support mobility and feeding.

cards.title: Clinical Scenario: Applying Your Knowledge
cards.body: CASE STUDY

bullets.label: Two hours after birth, a woman reports feeling
bullets.text: Two hours after birth, a woman reports feeling dizzy. Her maternity pad is rapidly saturating with blood. She appears pale and her pulse is elevated.

bullets.label: Immediately assess uterine tone — is the uterus boggy or firm?
Check and record vital signs; note the degree of blood loss.
Call for urgent assistance; activate the PPH response protocol.
Perform uterine massage if indicated per local guidelines.
Remain with the woman, provide reassurance and document all interventions.

cards.title: Key Takeaways & Safe Discharge
cards.body: Before discharge, ensure the woman and her support people are prepared, informed and confident.

bullets.label: Assess lochia and uterine involution regularly throughout the postnatal stay.
Treat Heavy Bleeding as an Emergency
Never delay escalation. Swift action saves lives.
Address both physiological needs and psychological wellbeing at every interaction.
With the mother's consent, involve family in
bullets.text: With the mother's consent, involve family in discharge education so everyone knows the warning signs and how to seek help.

decks.title: Essential Newborn Assessment and Care
decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 6 - Level 1 - Section 4 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Section 4: Essential Newborn Assessment and Care
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS) · Program 6 · Level 1 – Qualified Nurse

cards.title: Introduction
cards.body: The moment of birth marks a profound physiological shift. The newborn must rapidly adapt to:

bullets.label: Nurses are central to supporting this
bullets.text: Nurses are central to supporting this transition, performing systematic assessment and educating families in safe newborn care.

bullets.label: Establishing independent respiration outside the uterus
Regulating body heat in a new environment
Initiating feeding and transitioning cardiovascular function

cards.title: LEARNING OUTCOMES
cards.body: What You Will Be Able to Do

bullets.label: Conduct both immediate and ongoing systematic newborn assessment with confidence
Facilitate thermoregulation, feeding readiness and mother–baby bonding
Distinguish expected transitional findings from those requiring clinical concern
Escalate urgent neonatal findings promptly and appropriately

cards.title: CORE CONCEPT 1
cards.body: Immediate Adaptation at Birth

bullets.label: Initial care is structured around five priorities to support the newborn's transition to extra-uterine life:
Clear and maintain a patent airway
Observe rate, effort and air entry
Assess heart rate, colour and perfusion
Prevent heat loss from the first moment
Apgar scoring supports but does not replace assessment

cards.title: CORE CONCEPT 2
cards.body: Thermoregulation

bullets.label: Newborns lose body heat rapidly through
bullets.text: Newborns lose body heat rapidly through evaporation, conduction, convection and radiation. Cold stress increases the risk of hypoglycaemia, respiratory distress and metabolic acidosis.

bullets.label: Remove wet linen without delay at birth
Place on mother's chest; promotes warmth and bonding
Ensure room temperature and clothing are appropriate

cards.title: CORE CONCEPT 3
cards.body: Feeding and Routine Care

bullets.label: Assess readiness cues, latch and attachment, swallowing and adequate output (wet and soiled nappies)
Clean and inspect the umbilical cord stump per local policy; monitor for signs of infection
Administer recommended prophylaxis (e.g. Vitamin K) and immunisations in accordance with local guidelines

cards.title: CORE CONCEPT 4
cards.body: Warning Signs Requiring Urgent Review

bullets.label: Never assume abnormal findings are due to normal newborn sleepiness. Escalate promptly when you observe:
Central cyanosis, grunting, nasal flaring or chest retractions
Persistent hypothermia unresponsive to warming measures
Poor feeding, marked lethargy or abnormal muscle tone
Seizures, jaundice within 24 hours, or any signs of infection

cards.title: CLINICAL EXAMPLE
cards.body: Applying Knowledge at the Bedside

bullets.label: A newborn appears sleepy, feeds poorly and has a low temperature. The nurse does not assume normal sleepiness.
Skin-to-skin or warm environment; remove wet linen
Observe respiratory rate, effort and skin perfusion
Document findings and communicate using ISBAR or local framework

cards.title: Newborn Assessment: Key Steps at a Glance
cards.body: Immediate Care

bullets.label: This four-step framework guides nurses from the
bullets.text: This four-step framework guides nurses from the moment of birth through to safe ongoing newborn care, ensuring no critical assessment step is missed.

cards.title: KEY LEARNING POINTS
cards.body: Section Summary

bullets.label: Dry immediately, promote skin-to-skin and ensure a warm environment
Evaluate breathing, colour, tone and feeding at every assessment
Know transitional findings versus warning signs requiring escalation
Teach parents when and how to seek urgent help for their newborn
Prepare for NCLEX: Expect scenario-based
bullets.text: Prepare for NCLEX: Expect scenario-based questions on newborn assessment priorities, Apgar interpretation and thermoregulation interventions.
